Section 279.50, subsection 10, paragraph b, Code 7 2025, is amended to read as follows: 8 b. “Research-based” means all of the following: 9 (1) Complete complete, unbiased information that is 10 verified or supported by the weight of research conducted 11 in compliance with accepted scientific methods ; , recognized 12 as medically accurate and objective by leading professional 13 organizations and agencies with relevant expertise in the 14 field, such as the American college of obstetricians and 15 gynecologists, the American public health association, the 16 American academy of pediatrics, and the national association of 17 school nurses; and published in peer-reviewed journals where 18 appropriate. 19 (2) Information that is free of racial, ethnic, sexual 20 orientation, and gender biases. 21 EXPLANATION 22 The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with 23 the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly. 24 This bill incorporates provisions related to pregnancy and 25 fetal development into the human growth and development and 26 health curricula provided by school districts, accredited 27 nonpublic schools, charter schools, and innovation zone schools 28 to students enrolled in grades 1 through 12. 29 The bill requires that the human growth and development 30 curricula provided by school districts, nonpublic schools, 31 charter schools, and innovation zone schools in grades 1 32 through 8, and the health curriculum in grades 9 through 12, 33 include instruction related to human development inside the 34 womb. If interpretive rulemaking 9 authority is clearly vested in the discretion of an agency by 10 statute, the applicable judicial standard of review is whether 11 the rules constitute an irrational, illogical, or wholly 12 unjustifiable interpretation of law by the agency (Code section 13 17A.19(10)(l)). If interpretive rulemaking authority is not 14 clearly vested in the discretion of an agency, the applicable 15 judicial standard of review is whether the rules constitute an 16 erroneous interpretation of law (Code section 17A.19(10)(c)). 17 The bill modifies the definition of “research-based” for 18 purposes of human growth and development instruction, and for 19 purposes of the state’s educational program, to provide that 20 such term means complete, unbiased information that is verified 21 or supported by the weight of research conducted in compliance 22 with accepted scientific methods, recognized as medically 23 accurate and objective by leading professional organizations 24 and agencies with relevant expertise in the field, and 25 published in peer-reviewed journals where appropriate. 26 -5- LSB 1624XC (3) 91 jda/jh 5/ 5
